diagnosis: Serous borderline tumour
legend: Papillae are architecturally complex, with hierarchical branching.

diagnosis: Serous borderline tumour
legend: Papillae are lined by stratified epithelium with detached small clusters of tumour cells.

diagnosis: Micropapillary serous borderline tumour
legend: Micropapillary architecture is prominent.

diagnosis: Micropapillary serous borderline tumour
legend: Elongated micropapillae directly emanate from a large papilla, producing the so-called Medusa head appearance.

diagnosis: Microinvasion in a serous borderline tumour
legend: Small nests and individual tumour cells with abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm (arrows) are present within spaces devoid of epithelial lining in the stroma. This is the most common pattern of microinvasion.

diagnosis: Microinvasive low-grade serous carcinoma
legend: Crowded small and medium-sized papillae in clear lacunar spaces (< 5 mm in greatest extent) are similar to the morphology of an invasive low-grade serous carcinoma.

diagnosis: Endosalpingiosis
legend: Epithelial stratification, cell tufting/detachment, and papillary architecture of epithelial-type non-invasive implants are absent. Endosalpingiosis does not qualify as advanced-stage in the setting of an ovarian serous borderline tumour.

diagnosis: Epithelial-type non-invasive implants associated with ovarian serous borderline tumour
legend: Complex papillary architecture is present within an epithelium-lined space.

diagnosis: Epithelial-type non-invasive implants associated with ovarian serous borderline tumour
legend: Papillae contain cells with low-grade nuclear features. Psammoma bodies are present.

diagnosis: Desmoplastic non-invasive implants associated with ovarian serous borderline tumour
legend: Low-grade simple glands with slight epithelial stratification are present within abundant desmoplastic stroma.

diagnosis: Desmoplastic non-invasive implants associated with ovarian serous borderline tumour
legend: Individual epithelial cells (arrows) are present within abundant desmoplastic stroma. This finding does not fulfil the criteria for invasive implants.

diagnosis: Invasive implants associated with ovarian serous borderline tumour
legend: There is destructive infiltration of underlying tissue. Small papillae and micropapillae are markedly crowded and haphazardly arranged. The histological appearance is akin to that of invasive low-grade serous carcinoma.

diagnosis: Invasive implants associated with ovarian serous borderline tumour
legend: Small papillae and micropapillae are present within clear lacunar spaces and demonstrate low-grade atypia. Psammoma bodies are also seen.

diagnosis: Low-grade serous neoplasm
legend: Papillary structures with relatively uniform small cells and low-grade nuclear atypia.

diagnosis: Serous borderline tumour
legend: Peritoneal fluid cytology. Note papillae with mild epithelial atypia encompassing a psammoma body.

diagnosis: Serous borderline tumour
legend: Peritoneal fluid cytology. Note the 3D epithelial clusters with mild epithelial atypia and discernible nucleoli.

diagnosis: Serous borderline tumour in a pelvic lymph node
legend: Papillary proliferation of bland serous epithelium and psammoma bodies, at the left. There is also endosalpingiosis involving this node, at the right.

diagnosis: Serous borderline tumour of the ovary
legend: Papillae with hierarchical branching architecture lined by low cuboidal/columnar cells with minimal cytologic atypia. Cell detachment and tufting are identified.

diagnosis: Serous borderline tumour of the ovary with a micropapillary pattern
legend: Tumour with non-hierarchical architecture in which micropapillae emanate directly from large papillary cores. The micropapillae are at least 5 times long as they are wide. This area should measure at least 5mm in one linear dimension.

diagnosis: Serous borderline tumour of the ovary with a cribriform pattern
legend: Serous borderline tumour with cribriform pattern showing punched out spaces resulting from epithelial proliferation and fusion of papillae.
